title: Quebec Elects a Party That Wants Independence From Canada
summary:
Voters in Quebec, a province in Canada, chose a new government in an election on Monday. The Parti Québécois, or PQ, is projected to have won enough seats to form a minority government. A minority government has the most seats but not more than half, so it needs help from other parties to pass its plans.

The PQ wants Quebec to become independent, or separate from the rest of Canada. It has promised to hold a public vote, called a referendum, on that question. This is the first time the PQ has been in power since 2014. Its leader, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, is set to become Quebec's new premier, which is like a governor in the United States.

In his victory speech, St-Pierre Plamondon talked about his independence plans. He said, "Our national destiny will be achieved one day." He also promised to be "the premier of everyone in Quebec." He has said a referendum would happen only after President Donald Trump leaves office. The United States and Canada are in a trade dispute over Trump's tariffs, which are taxes on imported goods.

It is not clear how the PQ could hold a referendum. The rival parties it would need for support are against independence.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney congratulated St-Pierre Plamondon. Carney said, "Building a stronger Quebec is at the heart of our mission to build a stronger Canada." The result could still lead to disagreements between Quebec and Canada's national government over issues such as immigration and the monarchy. St-Pierre Plamondon has promised to "abolish the monarchy in Quebec" and use that money for social services instead.

The party that ran Quebec before, the Coalition Avenir Québec, is not projected to have won a single seat.
why_it_matters: The result could test Canada's unity and lead to disagreements between Quebec and Canada's national government over immigration and the monarchy.

background_read: Canada is divided into provinces, and each province elects its own government to handle matters such as schools and health care.
Quebec is a mostly French-speaking province, and the Parti Québécois has long argued that it should become its own country.
A referendum is a vote in which all citizens answer one question directly, such as whether Quebec should separate from Canada.
In a minority government, the leading party has fewer than half the seats, so it needs votes from rival parties to pass its plans.
